title: Word RAM decider yields polynomial-time class bound
statement: Let $P$ be an extended word RAM program and $L$ a language of Boolean strings. Suppose there are natural-number-valued functions $W,TW,SW$ such that $W$ is computable by a finite Turing machine within time $TW(n)$ and space $SW(n)$, and for every Boolean string $x$ there is an output string $o$ for which $P$, on $x$ with empty coin sequence and word width $W(|x|)$, halts within $T(|x|)$ steps and space $F(|x|)$, returning the Boolean indicator of membership in $L$. If $T':\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ and $a\in\mathbb{N}$ satisfy, for every $n$, $TW(n)+(T(n)+1)(F(n)(W(n)+1)+W(n)^2+n+1)\le aT'(n)$, then $L$ belongs to the deterministic time class with bound $T'$.
